We have a target molecule: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This appears to be a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone? Actually structure: methyl ester of a bicyclic lactone? Let's decode: COC( ... )=O is a methyl ester attached to carbonyl. Inside: [C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O. That's a bicyclic system (maybe a bicyclo[2.2.1]?). Looks like a Diels-Alder adduct (bicyclic). The hint says Diels-Alder reaction is forward. So retrosynthesis: break the bicyclic ring via retro Diels-Alder to give a diene and a dienophile. The template 264054 is a retro Diels-Alder? Let's examine retro_smarts_template: '[C:1]-[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]>>[C:1]-[CH2;D2;+0:2]-[CH2;D2;+0:3]-[C:4]'. This is a retro Diels-Alder converting a double bond to two single bonds (i.e., breaking a cyclohexene to a diene). So applying this template to target should give precursors: a diene (with two double bonds) and a dienophile? Actually the template seems to break a C=C double bond within a 4-carbon chain? The product side is a cyclohexene? The retro transforms a C=C into two CH2 groups. So applying to our target will give a linear precursor.

We need to propose a route with 1 reaction (retro Diels-Alder). So we need to apply template 264054 to target to get precursors. Use apply_template tool.
